appearance.title: Appearance
appearance.description: How the app is dressed, and which language it speaks to you in. Both choices are remembered and apply right away, with no restart.

theme.name: Theme
theme.why: Light is the original. Night is not its negative: black is never pure there, a blue veil runs through every surface, and the accent goes down rather than up. For bright screens and late sessions.

language.name: Language
language.why: The language of the interface. Your track, artist and album names come from your files, so they stay as they are. With no explicit choice, the app follows your system's language.

launchWelcome.name: Welcome at launch
launchWelcome.why: Once the environment check is done, Sonarche takes a second to say hello before opening the window. Turn it off and the app goes straight in — the fade between the two stays either way.

tour.name: Guided tour
tour.why: The interface's landmarks, in six steps. Replay it any time.

adding.title: Downloading & importing
adding.description: The two pages that fill the ark: what is already unfolded when you get there, and the pause the app keeps between two downloads.

downloadOptions.name: Unfold the options when a link is pasted
downloadOptions.why: As soon as a link is recognised, the panel opens on the download's destination and category. Turn it off if you know your settings — the chevron is still there to open them case by case.

importOptions.name: Unfold the options once a folder is scanned
importOptions.why: Once the folder is read, the panel opens on the import's grouping and category. Turn it off if you always import the same way.

delay.name: Delay between two downloads
delay.why: On a playlist, tracks are fetched one by one. This pause spaces the requests out so long batches stay within the source's rate limits instead of triggering 403 errors. The real delay is randomised between this value and twice it.
delay.estimate: For a {{count}}-track playlist, the pauses add about {{duration}}.
delay.warning: Below one second the requests run back to back with almost no pause — which is exactly the behaviour that gets a client spotted and handed 403s halfway through a long playlist. Three seconds is the safe setting.

metadata.title: Metadata
metadata.description: How the app mentions what it could still complete, and how carefully the automatic identification rewrites your tags.

badges.name: Badge on the Metadata tab
badges.why: Shows how many tracks and albums are left to complete in the sidebar — the same count the Metadata page delivers, and the page carries this switch too. Turn it off if you would rather visit the page at your own pace.

rematchConfirm.name: Ask before a re-match
rematchConfirm.why: A re-match queries MusicBrainz again and rewrites every tag it recognises, including your manual fixes. With this on, the app asks for confirmation before starting, on a track as on an album.

checks.name: Active checks
checks.why: The eight checks the app knows how to raise: missing year, no artwork, off-tree genre, duplicate… Each switches off on its own, and a check that is off leaves the queue and the badge without losing its count. They live on the Metadata page, next to what there is to fix.

files.title: Files
files.description: Where the app keeps your music on this disk, and what your files are made of.

location.name: Location
location.why: Pick the parent folder: the app creates and manages its own "Sonarche" folder inside it. What is there now moves with it — nothing is left behind.

move.title: Move the library?
move.body: All your music moves to this folder. The index stays valid: nothing is re-imported and nothing is identified again.
move.consequences: Playback stops and the app restarts once the transfer is done.

refusal.intoItself: That folder is inside the library, so the library cannot move into it. Pick one outside.
refusal.insideAppData: That folder belongs to the app's internal data, which "Erase everything" is allowed to delete. Your music does not belong there.
refusal.occupied: A "Sonarche" folder is already there and it is not empty. Empty it, or pick another parent.
refusal.notWritable: The app cannot write into that folder.
refusal.busy: A download or an import is running. Wait for it to finish: moving the files while something is writing into them would break them.

audioFormat.name: Audio file format
audioFormat.why: What your tracks are actually made of. By default Sonarche stores the audio exactly as it arrives: nothing is decoded or recompressed. Pick something else if your gear needs it — that costs a real re-encode, and quality nothing brings back.

m4a.name: Original (AAC · m4a)
m4a.why: The stream as it arrives, stored untouched. No added loss, no CPU time. The recommended setting, and the only free one.

mp3.name: MP3
mp3.why: The format everything reads: car stereo, old player, a USB stick plugged into a hi-fi. Worse than AAC byte for byte, but “worse” is not the question when the alternative is silence.

flac.name: FLAC
flac.why: Lossless — but lossless of an original that already lost something. Files 4 to 6 times bigger, for exactly the same sound. Only worth it if a device insists on FLAC.

convert.pitchNative: The setting only applies to future downloads. If your library still holds files converted at some point, you can put them all back to the original format.
convert.pitch: The setting only applies to future downloads. What is already on disk stays as it is — unless you convert the whole library to {{format}}.
convert.title: Convert everything to {{format}}?
convert.intro: Every file that is not already {{format}} will be re-encoded, then the original deleted. Tags, covers and filing are untouched.

warnings.time: This takes a while: a few seconds of CPU per track, so hours on a large library.
warnings.blocked: Sonarche stays on this window for the whole run. No browsing, no listening, no downloading.
warnings.quality: A re-encode loses quality, and a second conversion loses more. None of it comes back.

convert.running: Converting to {{format}}. Leave this window open.
convert.skipped: {{count}} track(s) were already in the right format and were left alone.
convert.failed: {{count}} track(s) could not be converted — they are intact, in their original format.

services.title: External services
services.description: The services the app asks to identify your music: the key one of them wants, whether they all answer, and how fast it is allowed to ask. Keys are stored in the system keychain, never in a file.

acoustid.name: AcoustID
acoustid.why: Identifies a track by its acoustic fingerprint (the audio itself, not its name). This is what finds the right studio version of a song and automatically fills in album, year, track number and cover art. Free key at acoustid.org.
acoustid.savedDetail: Future imports can now identify your tracks by their fingerprint.

testReason.invalidKey: The service does not recognise this key. Check that you copied the application key rather than the account id.
testReason.empty: There is no key to test.
testReason.unknown: The service refused it without saying why.

health.name: Service status
health.why: Nothing is sent until you click. When an import comes back with no cover or no genre, the answer is often here.
health.failed: The check could not start. The Python environment may not be ready.

fixed.title: Metadata services' pace
fixed.body: AcoustID and Last.fm are reached through keys every install shares: one rushed user can get the key throttled for everyone. The app sets the pace itself, and it is not adjustable.

advanced.title: Advanced
advanced.description: The log to send when something goes wrong, and the engine to rebuild when it stops answering. Nothing here touches your music.

logs.name: Diagnostic log
logs.why: What the app and its engine report while they work. This is the file to send along when something goes wrong.

reinstall.name: Reinstall the environment
reinstall.why: Deletes the Python environment and the downloaded tools, then rebuilds them on restart. Leaves your music, your index and your history alone. Worth trying when the app refuses to import or download for no clear reason.
reinstall.dialogBody: The app deletes its Python engine and restarts into the first-run walkthrough to rebuild it. This takes a few minutes and none of your data is involved.

danger.title: Danger zone
danger.description: Permanent deletions. Nothing here can be undone: there is no trash, no backup and no way back.

eraseLibrary.name: Delete the library
eraseLibrary.why: Deletes every audio file from the disk along with its index. Artist images, playlists (emptied, but kept) and the histories stay in place.
eraseLibrary.dialogBody: This is permanent. Here is what goes:
eraseLibrary.itemFiles: Every audio file in the library, deleted from the disk
eraseLibrary.itemIndex: The beets index: titles, albums, artists, genres, artwork
eraseLibrary.itemPlaylists: The playlists' contents — the lists themselves remain, empty
eraseLibrary.keeps: Artist images, playlist names and the histories are kept.

eraseArtistImages.name: Delete artist images
eraseArtistImages.why: Deletes every artist image placed by hand. There is no automatic source: they will not come back on their own.
eraseArtistImages.dialogBody: This is permanent. Here is what goes:
eraseArtistImages.itemFiles: Every artist image, deleted from the disk
eraseArtistImages.keeps: The generated avatars take over; nothing else is touched.

erasePlaylists.name: Delete playlists
erasePlaylists.why: Deletes every playlist, their covers and their M3U8 files. The music is not touched.
erasePlaylists.dialogBody: This is permanent. Here is what goes:
erasePlaylists.itemLists: Every playlist, including the favorites' contents
erasePlaylists.itemCovers: Their covers and their M3U8 files
erasePlaylists.keeps: The music and the rest of the library stay put.

eraseHistory.name: Delete the histories
eraseHistory.why: Empties the download history and the import history. Music already in the library is not touched.
eraseHistory.dialogBody: This is permanent. Here is what goes:
eraseHistory.itemDownloads: The history of finished, failed or cancelled downloads
eraseHistory.itemUndo: The ability to undo a past import goes with its history
eraseHistory.keeps: The music and in-flight downloads stay put.

erase.name: Erase everything
erase.why: Empties the whole library and restores default settings — the install and your AcoustID key stay in place. Your audio files are deleted from the disk. There is no bin, no undo and no backup.
erase.dialogBody: This is permanent. Here is what goes:
erase.itemFiles: Every audio file in the library, deleted from the disk
erase.itemIndex: The beets index: titles, albums, artists, genres, artwork
erase.itemPlaylists: Playlists and their M3U8 files, artist and playlist images
erase.itemHistory: The download and import history, and pending downloads
erase.itemKeys: Your settings, back to their defaults, and the diagnostic log
erase.keepsEngine: The Python environment and your AcoustID key are kept: the app is usable again straight away, no setup to redo.

developer.title: Developer tools
developer.description: Only visible in development builds. These tools are for testing the app, not for using it.

resetSetup.name: Replay the setup
resetSetup.why: Puts back what the app can rebuild on its own, so the first-run walkthrough can be gone through again. Leaves your audio files and the beets index alone.
resetSetup.done: Reset. Restart the app to start over.

apiKeys.label: AcoustID key
apiKeys.cost: you'll have to paste it back

resetLibrary.name: Delete the library
resetLibrary.why: Destructive: deletes every audio file in the library and the beets database, for a clean slate between test runs.
resetLibrary.warning: Every library file and the beets index will be permanently deleted.

toasts.name: Notification preview
toasts.why: The strips the app raises in the bottom right corner. Each button fires one and does nothing else: no operation starts, nothing is left to undo. It is the only way to look at their layout without provoking a real download or a real failure.

success.label: Success
success.title: Key saved
success.body: The next imports will be able to identify your tracks by their fingerprint.

danger.label: Error
danger.title: The download failed
danger.body: The source refused the request (403). Try again in a few minutes.

warning.label: Warning
warning.title: No artwork found
warning.body: The track arrived fine, but no service offered an image.

long.label: Long text
long.title: The engine did not answer
long.body: Traceback (most recent call last): File "beetsplug/sonarche_import.py", line 214, in run — sqlite3.OperationalError: database is locked. The Python environment may be reinstalling; try again once the progress strip is gone.
